title: Coining Words and Concepts
grammar: Deverbal action nouns (-ás/-és) and deadjectival abstract nouns (-ság/-ség)
goal: I can derive action and result nouns from verbs using -ás/-és.
I can derive abstract quality nouns from adjectives and nouns using -ság/-ség.
I can discuss literary style, originality, and mannerisms using B2 critical vocabulary.

sections.title: Unit 3: Language, Style & Word Formation
body: Hungarian is extraordinarily transparent in how it builds abstract concepts: from almost any verb you can derive an action noun with -ás/-és, and from almost any adjective or noun a quality/state noun with -ság/-ség. In essays, criticism, and journalism, these nominalizations link into possessive chains ('a szöveg átfogalmazásának a fontossága').

Guided by Frigyes Karinthy's brilliant 1912 collection of literary parodies Így írtok ti ('That's How You Write'), you will learn both how to construct sophisticated nominalized chains and how to unpack over-stuffed bureaucratic or pretentious prose into crisp verbal Hungarian.
